title: Re-enable Java compiler warnings and add static analysis
description:
The Java build currently has no dedicated static analysis step in `make check`, and the root `pom.xml` still has the compiler warning flag commented out:
- `pom.xml` comments out `<compilerArgument>-Xlint:all</compilerArgument>`.
- There is no Checkstyle, SpotBugs, Error Prone, or similar plugin wired into the standard check flow.

This repo is already relying on Maven test/build validation, but that leaves obvious warning-level problems and API misuse patterns invisible until runtime or review. Tightening this should start with the lowest-risk step:
1. Re-enable a conservative `javac` warning set first, likely `-Xlint:unchecked,deprecation` rather than full `-Xlint:all` on day one.
2. Measure the warning volume module-by-module, especially around `Mage.Client.Bridge` where MCP-related changes land.
3. Once warning volume is understood, add a real static analysis tool to `make check` if the false-positive rate is acceptable.

This is worth doing, but it is not a one-line config flip because the current warning backlog is unknown.
